q1.answer: The correct set is only the call expressions ref(...) that create a reactive ref in vuejs/core packages/reactivity/src. The oracle = the structural (AST) call-expression count + file list on the frozen SHA (compute at run time by materializing the subtree and running a structural pattern ref($$$)). A plain text search over-counts by including non-call occurrences: e.g. import lines (`import { ref } from ...`), the substring inside longer identifiers like shallowRef/refIndex/isRef, type annotations, and comment/JSDoc mentions.
q1.scoring: 1.0 = enumerates call sites via structural/AST (not raw text) AND names a concrete non-call false positive AND (c) states the method distinction plus a plausible raw-text hit count showing the over-count; 0.5 = right files but count includes text-only noise, or (b)/(c) vague; 0 = only a raw text count with no AST distinction.
q1.capabilityPoint: Octocode has AST structural search; gh CLI has text search only -- this is the core gap. Grader must confirm Arm B used a structural/AST query, not a text count.
q1.expectedWorkflow: ghCloneRepo(or remote structural) -> localSearchCode mode:structural `ref($$$)` -> contrast with text-mode count. Feature: AST vs text.

q2.answer: isTypeAssignableTo(source, target) checks assignability and delegates to the internal relation checker isTypeRelatedTo(source, target, assignableRelation) (the shared engine also used by isTypeComparableTo / isTypeSubtypeOf). Octocode reads just the function via localGetFileContent matchString:'function isTypeAssignableTo' (or ghGetFileContent matchString) transferring a few hundred chars; gh api returns the whole multi-MB file unless the agent hand-computes a line range.
q2.scoring: 1.0 = names isTypeRelatedTo + assignableRelation AND reports a small transfer achieved by a matched slice; 0.5 = correct delegation but pulled the whole file; 0 = wrong delegate or could not isolate the function.
q2.capabilityPoint: matchString slice + minify vs raw whole-file dump -- token cost differentiator.
q2.expectedWorkflow: ghGetFileContent matchString:'isTypeAssignableTo' contextLines (targeted slice) -- NOT fullContent. Feature: matchString-anchored partial fetch on a multi-MB file.

Oracle = its real files-changed count, net additions/deletions, source-vs-test split, the largest-diff source file, AND the motivating behavior/bug grounded in the diff hunks or linked issue (judge re-reads the diff + linked issue), fetched via api.github.com. Octocode: ghSearchPullRequests prNumber:<n> reviewMode:full. gh: gh pr view <n> --json files,additions,deletions + gh pr diff.
q3.scoring: 1.0 = correct file count + net delta + source/test split + largest source file + motivation grounded in a cited diff hunk or linked issue; 0.5 = stats right but motivation is a title paraphrase, or 3-4 of 5 right; 0 = wrong PR, fabricated stats, or fabricated issue link.
q3.capabilityPoint: Both can do this; measure token cost of the diff read (Octocode selected-patch vs gh full JSON).
q3.expectedWorkflow: ghSearchPullRequests filters (repo, merged, path lib/) -> prNumber reviewMode:full for files/stats/diff hunks. Feature: PR search + selective diff read.

q10.answer: (a) spawn -> ChildProcess.prototype.spawn / exports.spawn in lib/child_process.js. (b) execFileSync in lib/child_process.js (spawnSync-backed). (c) normalizeSpawnArguments is an internal helper in lib/child_process.js. All three live in the same file, so Octocode reads it once (cache/local) and answers all three; a gh-only agent tends to issue 3 separate `gh search code` calls, pressuring the ~10 req/min code-search limit. Oracle = all three correctly located + an honest count of code-search API calls spent.
q10.scoring: 1.0 = all three correctly located AND reports its code-search call count / rate-limit handling honestly; 0.5 = 2/3 located or vague on call count; 0 = wrong locations.
q10.capabilityPoint: Session cache + local routing reduce repeated GitHub calls; gh re-hits the API each time.
q10.expectedWorkflow: Multiple ghSearchCode queries batched via queries[] + session cache; count code-search API calls vs gh's per-invocation hits. Feature: batching + caching under the 10/min limit.
